newsitem.title: CHINA: HK red chip index futures/options expected in Sept.
newsitem.headline: HK red chip index futures/options expected in Sept.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) will launch red-chip index futures and options together in September, a source close to the exchange said on Tuesday.
"The futures and options will be based on the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index and launched sometimes in September," the source told Reuters.
The HKFE would announce the decision on Wednesday, he added.
The Hang Seng red chip index, monitoring the movement of shares in 32 Hong Kong-listed companies with Chinese financial backing, was launched on June 16.
A HKFE spokesman declined to comment on the launch but confirmed the exchange will hold a news briefing on Wednesday.

HKFE chief executive Ivers Riley said earlier this year that China-related stock index futures and options would be launched simultaneously probably in the second half of 1997 following the success of Hang Seng Index options. He said the real attraction in Asia was the growth in China and the best way to introduce China-related products was when people cared.

The HKFE and the stock exchange said in June that they would start trading of stock futures and options on the shares of two red chips -- China Resouces Enterprises Ltd and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd -- on July 14.
